about: Global policies (#5308): rules that ship with MaximizePM and apply to the sessions of every user's queue. Each has an id (g1, g2, ...; never reuse one), the rule (text), its reason, its source (who decided it, and when), and an optional role: one role or a list of roles (worker, reviewer, deployer, owner, manager, expert; none: every session). They change only by a commit and a release. A person's own rules are user policies in their queue (maxpm policy add), never here.

policies.text: The manager works for the user: bring the user nothing that the manager can answer. A worker asks the manager first, and goes to the user only for what the manager cannot decide (a decision or approval only the user can give, an account, payment or legal step). The manager answers each question itself when it can, and sends on to the user only what it cannot answer.
policies.reason: The point of MaximizePM is less work for the user: the user sees only what the manager cannot answer. #5307 enforces this in code: a question from a session to a person goes to the active manager first, and reaches the person only when the manager neither answers nor forwards it within question_hold (10m).

policies.text: Before you put a decision to the person (or add a person item with a decision), run maxpm search on the subject with --status done and read the recent decisions. When an earlier answer covers it, close the item and quote that answer; otherwise ask only what it leaves open, and name the earlier answer.
policies.reason: A question the person already answered costs their time and their trust in the queue.

policies.text: When the person must approve or decide, put the thing itself in the message: the exact text, a screenshot, the old and the new code, what each option does. A link with 'yes?' is not enough.
policies.reason: The person can answer at once only when they see what they approve.

policies.text: When you add an item for a later day, hold it in the same step: make it a person's item (--doer human), or run maxpm blocked <id> --until <time> right after the add.
policies.reason: A ready item goes to an idle session within seconds.

policies.text: Try a vendor sign-in or sign-up once. On any failure (an error, a CAPTCHA, a check, a wrong page), stop and ask the person with maxpm ask --blocked; never retry.
policies.reason: Retries hammer the vendor's site, can lock the account, and change the person's browser tab.

policies.text: Never look in environment variables or home-folder files for API keys, not even to see if one is there. Use the model the item names; when it names none, add a person item (--doer human --blocks <id>). A key that maxpm secret list names is given: use it by name (maxpm secret pipe or env), never print it.
policies.reason: A missing key is the person's step. A search for keys reads secrets the task was not given, and it ends at a permission prompt for the person.

policies.text: On a fault item (an operational item whose title starts with ops:) you investigate: read logs, state and the check's runs, find the cause, write it on the item, add fix items for the code (they go through the normal review and release), and close the item with the cause. Change nothing in production yourself; a repair runs only through maxpm ops repair.
policies.reason: A fault investigation starts at once, before a person looks; a guess that changes production can make the fault worse, while a found cause and fix items go through review. The monitor is deterministic, and the investigation is ordinary queue work (#5431, #5432).
